summary: Nix research program wave 1: three grounding audits (ocx index and fleet, exemplar flake shape, exemplar tool runs) and six landscape scouts over the Nix corpora

headline_numbers: 125 packages / 99 namespaces / 1720 stored image indexes in /home/mherwig/dev/index/p/
Tags per package: min 4, median 13, mean 23.9, max 135 (bazelbuild/bazel)
56.7% of all tags (1692/2985) share their content digest with another tag in the same package
Tag shapes: 41.0% full semver, 30.4% semver+date, 16.1% minor float, 4.9% major float, 4.2% latest, 3.4% other
status field: 100% active (0 deprecated, 0 yanked, 0 superseded_by) across all 125
root.schema.json's variants field: populated in 0/125 packages despite 36 variant-prefixed tags existing

10 distinct platform shapes over 9115 entries; 665 image-index files (31 packages) carry explicit os.features on linux vs 1170 files (104 packages) bare-only, with 12 packages appearing in both sets over time
artifactType: 100% application/vnd.sh.ocx.package.v1 (1720/1720); annotation coverage: source 98.3%, revision 97.2%, licenses 92.6% (128 indexes with none); no mainProgram-equivalent key anywhere

H6 CONFIRMED and sharper than hypothesized: ghcr.io manifest fetch is 401 bare / 200 with a free anonymous bearer token, but the blob itself 307-redirects to a SAS-signed, ~10-minute-expiring URL on pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com; nix-prefetch-url with no token fails with the same bare 401
actionlint's linux/amd64 binary: static Go ELF, no PT_INTERP, matching the doc's 'static binaries carry no os.features' rule

ocx: 17 -sys crates in Cargo.lock (aws-lc-sys, zstd-sys, liblzma-sys, clang-sys, etc.); grimoire: 10 (no clang-sys/compression sys crates); ocx-sdk-python: 0 native deps (dependencies=[]); setup-ocx: pure TS/bun, reimplements glibc/musl detection independently of ocx's own Rust code
top_smells: 56.7% tag/digest aliasing means naive tag-walking overcounts distinct builds 2-3x; must dedup by content digest first

Bare linux/amd64 and linux/amd64+libc.glibc can coexist as two separate manifests at different digests in the same image index (documented intentional scoring behavior, not a bug) — a naive (os,arch)-keyed generator picks the wrong manifest silently
clang-sys appears in ocx's Cargo.lock with no traced first-party consumer — an untraced native-toolchain surprise waiting for the first nix build attempt
setup-ocx (TypeScript) reimplements glibc/musl host detection that ocx's own Rust host_capabilities.rs already implements — duplicate knowledge across the fleet

The index repo's own docs (product-context.md) flag the desc-blob path's frozen-contract status as explicitly unresolved, yet it's the natural source for embedding README/logo content in a generated flake
patterns_worth_encoding: Canonicalize on content digest, treat tags as labels applied after — both ocx's own dependency-pinning rule (manifest digest, never index digest) and the tag-aliasing problem point the same direction for a generator's dedup logic

nixpkgs' dockerTools.pullImage/skopeo-based FOD fetching is the right prior art for the ghcr.io token+redirect dance (H6), not a plain fetchurl — the ocx-specific work is only the metadata.json-to-derivation translation layer on top

ocx's own docs already draw explicit Nix/Guix comparisons (propagatedBuildInputs for public/interface dependency visibility; content-addressed store analogy) — ready-made citations for an authoring skill rather than something to re-derive

ocx's platform-string grammar (os/arch[/variant][+feature,...], percent-escaped for round-tripping) is structurally close to an extended Nix system string plus a libc tag — worth a side-by-side mapping in the eventual nix-generated-flakes artifact
contradictions_of_frame: H6 is confirmed but underspecified in the frame: the harder blocker isn't the bearer token (a single free anonymous GET) but the blob URL's 307 redirect to a SAS-signed, minutes-expiring URL on a different host — any fixer must run the fetch inside the derivation build, not pre-resolve a constant URL

H7 remains only half-checked: the live probe (actionlint) turned out to be a static binary with no os.features, confirming the 'nothing needed' half but leaving the dynamic-glibc/autoPatchelfHook half untested despite the probe running to completion

The frame implicitly treats root.schema.json's variants field as a usable existing signal; measured across the full corpus it is populated in 0/125 packages, so no downstream design can rely on it today

headline_numbers: 36/37 exemplar repos have a root flake.nix (typst/typst has none — dropped Nix as of 2026-09-23)
stdenv.lib and cargoSha256: 0 occurrences anywhere in the 37-repo corpus — fully extinct

nixpkgs 26.11 has dropped x86_64-darwin support — confirmed live via `nix flake show` against nix-community/fenix's own pinned nixpkgs rev, throwing 'Nixpkgs 26.11 has dropped support for x86_64-darwin'; 17/37 exemplars hardcode that system string
Systems-handling strategy: flake-parts 12/37, nix-systems input 9/37, flake-utils 7/37, blueprint 5/37, hand-rolled genAttrs/forAllSystems 29/37 — no single strategy is a majority
Zero Nix CI jobs in the whole corpus run on a Windows runner (a naive grep false-positives on 'darwin' containing 'win')
11/37 (30%) declare nixConfig, all pointing at a Cachix-style cache only
Median nixpkgs-lock age 65 days, range 0 (llm-agents.nix) to 566 days (numtide/blueprint)
10/37 repos have zero git tags at all, including widely-depended-on ones (flake-parts, home-manager, nix-darwin)
flake-compat citations split three ways: edolstra/flake-compat (10, historical/redirected), NixOS/flake-compat (canonical), nix-community/flake-compat (maintained fork)
3 repos (DeterminateSystems x2, the-nix-way/dev-templates) consume FlakeHub as an input source via semver-range URLs, not only as a publish target
top_smells: 17/37 exemplars hardcode x86_64-darwin in systems lists against a nixpkgs branch that just dropped the platform (live-eval confirmed)
flake-compat fork fragmentation: majority still cite the historical edolstra/flake-compat rather than the canonical NixOS org location
flake.nix-only static scans undercount outputs for flake-parts/blueprint flakes (blueprint, treefmt, zed all show ~0 outputs despite exposing real ones via imported files)
Version-tag chaos: semver, bare semver, date-stamps, CI-bot timestamps, and zero tags all coexist with no dominant convention
All DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action CI uses pin the floating @main ref, unlike the SHA-pinning majority of cachix/install-nix-action users
nixConfig cache trust is one-size-fits-all (11 repos, all just a substituter+key pair, no additional trust controls or consumer guidance)
patterns_worth_encoding: numtide/llm-agents.nix's declarative passthru.updater schema (kind: github-source/npm/bun-github/platform/manifest/manifest-checksums, validated at nix flake check time) is close to ready-made prior art for ocx-index-to-flake generation
llm-agents.nix's ast-grep lint rules (no-unpinned-rev, prefer-tag-over-rev, no-legacy-sha256, use-formatelf, no-x86-64-darwin) are a template for a nix-quality rule set's enforceable checks

rust-overlay's positional hash-array compaction (_0.._N keyed to a shared targets.nix ordering) is a reusable trick for keeping large generated-flake data files small across many platform-repeated entries

Three distinct generated-flake data architectures exist in the wild (committed per-version generated .nix files; committed single-latest-snapshot JSON; committed raw upstream metadata + lazy per-entry fetch) — the ocx design should pick deliberately among them, not assume one
nixpkgs's own sanctioned IFD workaround ('commit generated intermediate files to version control', pkgs/README.md:525) is exactly what all three generated-flake architectures already do independently
stackbuilders/nixpkgs-terraform's builtins.warn-wrapped deprecated-attribute pattern is a low-ceremony way to rename generated attributes without an immediate break
contradictions_of_frame: H1 ('agents emit ~1000 instances of nixpkgs / dated idioms everywhere') does not hold at exemplar scale: worst offender for import-nixpkgs re-instantiation is 10 files (not 1000), and stdenv.lib/cargoSha256 are fully extinct (0 hits); surviving dated idioms are with-pkgs, rec{}, and hardcoded version literals, not the channel-era idioms H1 led with

H3 ('most flakes pass flake check but lack formatter/checks') is only partially true: just 14/37 repos even run nix flake check in CI, so pass/fail is unverified for the rest by this static pass; among the 14 that do, most also expose both formatter and checks, so the 'lacks formatter or checks' half applies to a minority, not a majority

H4 ('FlakeHub is the only semver-resolving channel') is contradicted on the consumption side — 3 repos consume FlakeHub as an input via its semver-range URL syntax, not only as a publish target; it is strongly supported on the versioning-practice side (10/37 repos have zero tags, and tag styles otherwise vary wildly)

New finding outside H1-H9: nixpkgs 26.11 has dropped x86_64-darwin support entirely, confirmed both by release-notes citation and by a live nix eval failure against an exemplar's own pinned nixpkgs rev — a dated, version-specific pitfall a static-only audit would have missed, though one exemplar's own lint rules (llm-agents.nix's no-x86-64-darwin.yml) had already anticipated it

headline_numbers: 27/36 (75%) exemplars declare no `formatter` output at all
statix 2230 / deadnix 1914 raw findings across 36 repos, but oxalica/nil alone is ~45%/32% of that (its own parser test fixtures, not code) — excluding it: 1111 statix / 1299 deadnix
flake-checker crashes outright (not "finds issues") on 4/36 repos: 3 with no top-level nixpkgs input, 1 with an empty flake.lock
nix flake check --no-build fails on cabal2nix IFD (cachix/cachix, cachix/devenv) and on the idiomatic self.packages.${system}.<name> default-package alias (confirmed on 2 independent repos)
nixConfig.extra-substituters is ignored by default on every one of 6/20 repos that declare it — H8 confirmed live
nixVersions.nix_2_24 is a stub throw in the pinned nixpkgs 26.11 unstable ("use nix_2_31") — the brief's own cross-version test plan is already stale
helix-editor/helix and DeterminateSystems/nix-installer time out at the 300s cap on flake show/check --all-systems; nix-installer hangs with zero output

Nixpkgs 26.11 unstable has dropped x86_64-darwin support outright (lib.trivial.throwIf at NixOS/nixpkgs@c7def046:lib/trivial.nix:1003), poisoning --all-systems results corpus-wide for reasons unrelated to the audited flake

Axis 1-3 (real nix flake metadata/show/check by remote ref): 20/36 repos measured — home-system check 14 pass/4 fail/2 timeout (70%), --all-systems check 8 pass/10 fail/2 timeout (40%), only 2/20 of the --all-systems failures are the flake's own authoring bug
top_smells: flake-checker's 11% (4/36) crash rate is silent — it throws a Rust Error to stderr and exits non-zero, indistinguishable from 'issues found' unless the caller inspects the message

oxalica/nil's own parser test fixtures (crates/syntax/test_data/parser/{err,ok}/) inflate the corpus-wide statix/deadnix counts by 30-45%; any blanket lint gate over 'every .nix file' must exclude test-fixture directories

nix flake check --no-build cannot validate the idiomatic self.packages.${system}.<name> default-package alias when evaluated from a remote github: ref (error: path '...-source' is not valid) — a very common authoring shape, not an edge case

--all-systems failures span 6 distinct root causes and only 2 of them (numtide/treefmt via blueprint's lib, helix's own pkgsFor helper) are the audited flake's fault; the rest are nixpkgs dropping a platform, IFD, a toolchain platform limit, an unsupported-platform dependency, and infinite recursion inside nixpkgs itself
nixConfig.extra-substituters in flake.nix is decorative for any consumer who hasn't opted in with --accept-flake-config, yet several exemplars ship it anyway
helix-editor/helix's ~100+ single-purpose tree-sitter-grammar flake inputs make its own evaluation network-bound, timing out nix flake show/check --all-systems at 300s purely on serial GitHub fetches
patterns_worth_encoding: Treat 'no formatter output' as the default finding for a nix-quality rule (75% miss rate), praising the exception rather than flagging the common case
Flag nixConfig in flake.nix as close to a no-op for first-time consumers in a nix-flake-release skill; tell authors to document substituters in README/CI instead

Give a nix-diagnose skill the verbatim-matchable crash/failure strings for flake-checker and nix flake check --no-build (no-nixpkgs-input crash, empty-lock crash, IFD 'is not valid', self-referential-src 'is not valid') so an agent recognizes 'known tool limitation' rather than 'something is broken'
Name the self.packages.${system}.<name> default-package alias explicitly as a known --no-build incompatibility in nix-quality, since it is the idiomatic way to write a default package

Carry an explicit --all-systems failure taxonomy in nix-quality/nix-diagnose rather than treating a flat pass/fail as ground truth — a flat count trains an agent to either over-trust green or over-react to red
For the ocx-index-generated-flake case: assume flake-checker will not run cleanly unless the generator emits a conventional top-level nixpkgs input, since ocx's index has no natural nixpkgs concept
contradictions_of_frame: H3 ('most exemplar flakes pass nix flake check --no-build on their home system') is directionally true but weaker than implied: 70% pass on the home system (not overwhelming), and only 40% pass under --all-systems — with the corpus's largest flakes (NixOS/nix, nix-darwin, home-manager, rust-overlay, disko) still unmeasured at time of writing

H9's concrete cross-version test plan (nixVersions.nix_2_24) is already stale: that exact attribute is a stub throw ('use nix_2_31') in the very nixpkgs revision the frame itself pins, so hardcoding a specific old-Nix version for compatibility guidance will rot within normal channel churn

H1 is not contradicted but is confirmed more concretely than the frame anticipated: import nixpkgs { inherit system; } is directly the cited cause of a live 2026 deprecation warning (56 hits from one repo alone), not just an aesthetic idiom; and H2's 'many nixpkgs instances' concern turned out to have a measured wall-clock cost (a real local build during cachix/devenv's cold eval, 95.6s) rather than only a lock-file-size cost the frame described

recent_shifts: `lib.fileset` is now nix.dev's taught default for source filtering, superseding `builtins.path`/`lib.sources.cleanSourceWith` filter-callback idioms most existing flakes still use.

`inputs.self.submodules`/`inputs.self.lfs` flake self-attributes (dated to Nix 2.27 by the NixOS wiki) remove the need for consumer-side `?submodules=1` URL params — a materially newer flake-schema feature.

RFC 0140 (pkgs/by-name, merged) and RFC 0166 (nixfmt as canonical formatter, merged) are both accepted changes that postdate a large fraction of existing community flakes/blog posts citing all-packages.nix placement or nixpkgs-fmt.
NixOS 26.05 introduced a `system.nix` entrypoint that loads NixOS configuration without a flake at all, explicitly positioned by nix.dev as equal-footing with flakes, not a lesser option.

Determinate Nix (Determinate Nix 3.0) unilaterally declared flakes 'stable' and shipped lazy trees/parallel evaluation/WASM support with no upstream equivalent, while Lix separately consolidated its own de-facto 'v1' flake feature set — confirms H9 directly from all three parties' current docs rather than by inference.

flake-checker's supported-branches list (0.2.15, measured) is itself a moving target (nixos-25.11/26.05 (+small) + unstable (+small) + darwin variants) that a CI policy must track release-over-release.

recent_shifts: nixfmt 1.3.0 (2026-05-26): the nixfmt-rfc-style package/attribute name was folded back into plain nixfmt; git-hooks.nix still exposes nixfmt-rfc-style as a separate legacy hook alias
nixfmt 1.4.0 (2026-07-07): introduced /*nixfmt:disable*/ /*nixfmt:enable*/ region-exclusion directive, the first sanctioned formatter escape hatch
nixfmt 1.5.0 (2026-09-10): fixed an exponential-parse-time bug on nested set-parameter defaults, present until 11 days before this survey

Nix 2.35 (2026-06-22): builtins.getFlake gained direct path support (builtins.getFlake ./subflake); source-to-store copying became lazier via hash-before-copy; nix flake check gained --print-out-paths
Determinate Nix 3.5.2 (stable/default by 2026-09-25): 'lazy trees' virtual-filesystem mechanism, not present in CppNix 2.35 or Lix, claimed 3x+ wall-time / 20x+ disk-usage wins
nixpkgs-vet ratchets (ongoing, RFC 140-era): strictDeps=true and __structuredAttrs=true are now enforced one-way for any new top-level package, closing off the old unset/false idiom for new code
Lix flake-stabilisation proposal (undated, living document): explicit intent to replace flake.lock with flake.lick/flake.lix and reconsider or drop the follows mechanism entirely
statix repository migration (as of 2026-09-27): canonical repo moved to a Tangled forge; nixpkgs' own statix package now builds from a Molybdenum Software fork, not oppiliappan/statix directly

recent_shifts: Determinate Nix 3.0 (2025-03-05) issued a unilateral 'formal stability guarantee for flakes' while upstream nix.dev still calls flakes experimental — the two positions are now openly contradicting, not merely unsettled.

Lazy trees (Determinate Nix 3.5.2+, upstream PR NixOS/nix#13225 still open) cut measured nixpkgs eval time 3x+ and disk use 20x+ but are not yet in CppNix — a live, dated CppNix/Determinate divergence.

Lix froze the flake feature set at Lix 2.94-2.95 (through 2026-03-25) and plans to extract flakes into a separate plugin, explicitly declining to ever stabilize them — a third, distinct position from both CppNix and Determinate.
lib.fileset (landed nixpkgs 23.11, argued for by Tweag 2023-11-28) supersedes lib.cleanSourceWith/builtins.filterSource as the recommended source-filtering mechanism.
Git LFS support in the flake git fetcher only landed around Nix 2.27 (2025-03-03); pre-2.27 consumers silently get LFS pointer files instead of content.
pkgs/by-name plus the nixpkgs-vet CI check is now nixpkgs' default new-top-level-package convention, superseding all-packages.nix-only guidance.

Magic Nix Cache's free CI-cache tier died 2025-02-01 when GitHub deprecated its underlying API (later partially restored by a community PR) — a documented, recent durability failure for vendor-dependent CI caching.

FlakeHub's rolling-release commit-count versioning and SemVer wildcard resolver were actively iterated through 2026 (flake-schemas interface changes dated March and June 2026) — the only flake versioning mechanism with real recent change; plain git-tag versioning has not changed.

A quadratic-time bug in flake.lock's input-naming collision search was discovered and fixed in 2026 (NixOS/nix#16387, ~21x speedup at 4,000 inputs) — directly relevant to any many-input generated flake and unknown to pre-2026 advice.

candidates.why: A flake's self is the git index, not the working tree, so an unstaged new file is silently absent with no error — the #1 confusion source for new flake users.
accept-flake-config = true is maintainer-confirmed to grant a flake root-equivalent command execution via nix.conf settings like post-build-hook, not merely relaxed cache trust.
Missing nixpkgs.follows across sibling inputs makes nix flake lock append _2, _3... name-collision suffixes (one real project reached ~1000), bloating lock files and splitting overlay reach.

nixpkgs review requires the hash= attribute (not sha256=), fetchFromGitHub over fetchgit over git://, and always a full commit hash since GitHub 404s on ambiguous short hashes and short-hash spam is a documented DoS vector.

nixpkgs's own new-package review template names the exact attributes reviewers check (meta.mainProgram, meta.license, meta.platforms, nativeBuildInputs, phase-hook wrapping, patch comments) — the codified form of recurring reviewer objections.

nix flake check evaluates every system's outputs even ones it cannot build locally, and IFD there can trigger a real foreign build attempt, producing a confusing wrong-platform error instead of a clean skip — open since 2020, still current on 2.35.

CVE-2026-39860 (critical) is a bypass of the earlier fix for CVE-2024-27297: a symlink at the FOD .tmp copy destination let any daemon user overwrite root-owned files for roughly two years before the follow-up advisory.

As of the 25.11/26.11 era pkgs.nixfmt is the stable RFC-166 formatter, pkgs.nixfmt-rfc-style is now the deprecated transitional name, pkgs.nixfmt-classic is pre-RFC-166, and nixpkgs-fmt is archived (2024-07-24) — most existing tutorials still say the reverse.

passthru.updateScript accepts a path, a derivation, or an attrset with command/attrPath, or simply nix-update-script {} — the mechanism that determines whether a package can be bumped by bot automation at all.

Relative path: and git+file:relative/path flake inputs still misbehave in nested subflake setups and regressed in nix flake archive on 2.26 — not a solved monorepo pattern despite being commonly recommended.

Lazy Trees (372 reactions, the highest in this corpus) changes what copying a flake input to the store means, is shipped in Determinate Nix 3.5, explicitly not adopted by Lix, and not yet in upstream CppNix 2.35.2.
A grep-able signature (nixpkgs_2, _3, ...) in flake.lock detects the duplicate-instance pathology before it reaches the scale seen in the 1000-instances case.
There is no first-class equivalent of fetchGit { submodules = true; } for a flake's own self — submodule content is invisible the same way untracked files are.
warn-dirty = false set in nixConfig is confirmed not always honored, so a published flake cannot reliably suppress the dirty-tree warning for its consumers via that mechanism.

A shallow-cloned CI checkout (e.g. GitHub Actions PR builds) makes Nix think a flake's own tree is dirty with no local changes at all — a CI-specific footgun with no upstream fix, only a checkout-configuration workaround.

Given accept-flake-config's confirmed root-equivalent-execution risk, whether a published flake should ever set nixConfig (even just extra-substituters) is a real publishing decision, not a style question.

Linux/Darwin and Python-version cargoHash divergence are documented, narrow, expected cases; true per-build nondeterminism is a distinct and rarer bug whose real fix is switching to cargoLock, not re-fetching the hash.
The only recorded real nixpkgs supply-chain incident (CVE-2024-3094) was handled by an immediate human revert PR same-day, not by any automated lock-file-level known-bad-version gate.

flake-checker's default check-outdated/check-owner/check-supported triad is real, but its own GitHub Action always exits 0 by design, so teams adopting it as a CI gate get a summary, not enforcement, unless they add their own gate.

meta.mainProgram has a mechanically checkable rule (set only when exactly one executable exists under bin/) with worked positive (ripgrep) and negative (e2fsprogs, polkit_gnome) examples straight from the nixpkgs README.

nixpkgs's own current idiom for a package needing to reference its own final derivation is finalAttrs.finalPackage inside stdenv.mkDerivation (finalAttrs: {...}), not a self-referential rec — sharper than H1's blanket avoid-rec framing.
Darwin SDK breakage (146 reactions) is its own recurring, maintainer-acknowledged, ongoing category driven by Apple's SDK distribution changes, distinct from ordinary hash-mismatch bugs.

Recent infinite-recursion cases are overwhelmingly module-system/overlay self-reference problems, not plain rec misuse, and nixpkgs is actively adding module-system error contexts specifically because the existing error is not actionable — directly refines H1.

FlakeHub is the only documented SemVer-resolving flake distribution channel in this corpus, requiring the literal git tag format v+SemVer for tagged releases versus a distinct rolling-release mode — directly tests H4.
FlakeHub's explicit publishing guidance is one flake per versioned artifact, not a monolithic flake bundling unrelated versioned things — directly informs the ocx-generated-flake artifact shape.

A named, credible contrarian source argues packages.${system} cannot express cross-compilation targets at all — worth verifying directly against nixpkgs's own cross docs rather than accepting either claim on faith.

An empirical cross-implementation study found real evaluation-level breakage differences across CppNix, Lix, and an alternative resolver for devShells/packages/checks outputs — a concrete way to falsify H9's severity.
Neither #4265's IFD-on-foreign-system failure nor the goldstein.lol implementation study support treating a green nix flake check as sufficient evidence a flake is publishable — directly tests H3.

statix's 17 confirmed lints (W01-W23) are Nix-language-level only; none check meta.* fields, nativeBuildInputs placement, or versionCheckHook — a real gap between lints-pass and review-ready that a rule must not conflate.
Confirmed exact statix lint IDs and names (W01 bool_comparison through W23 empty_list_concat) via direct toolchain run, needed for any rule that cites specific lint IDs.

deadnix's default behavior on lambda attrset pattern names would flag callPackage-style unused args unless --no-lambda-pattern-names is passed — a linter default that breaks the exact idiom nixpkgs packaging relies on.

home-manager's top-reaction issues are almost entirely feature gaps in the file-linking model (copy vs symlink, outOfStoreSymlink), signaling that a downstream module or generated config must never assume home.file targets are safely overwritable.

Whether config.allowUnfree/permittedInsecurePackages silently blocks flake evaluation in pure/--no-write-lock-file mode is named in the brief's exhaustive list but not yet confirmed with a planted fixture this wave.
Whether nix flake show/check catch a non-derivation value under packages.<system>.foo before a consumer's nix build fails at runtime is H3's core claim and remains unconfirmed by fixture this wave.

A generated flake pinning a content digest from an external index (the ocx case) faces the same integrity-risk class documented for GitHub's short-hash 404/rewrite precedent, plus ghcr.io's own token-gated blob trust boundary distinct from fetchFromGitHub.

follows has multiple still-open correctness bugs (segfault on self-follow, transitive-follows not resolved absolute, follows-removal ignoring the dependency's own lock) that argue for a minimal nix flake metadata check before trusting a lock file's follows graph.

Whether the now-stable pkgs.nixfmt reformats files identically to the transitional nixfmt-rfc-style, or produces a breaking diff on real code, is untested this wave and directly checkable with the available toolchain.

Whether the simple nix-update-script {} form suffices for the ocx-index-generated-flake use case, or the attrset command/attrPath form is required for a non-standard version source, directly informs the nix-generated-flakes artifact's update mechanism.

recent_shifts: Lazy trees (#6530, 372 reactions) redefines how flake inputs are copied to the store; shipped in Determinate Nix 3.5, explicitly not adopted by Lix, not yet in upstream CppNix 2.35.2 — invalidates any blanket 'flakes always fully copy inputs to the store' claim.

nixfmt reached stable RFC-166 status in the 25.11/26.11 era: pkgs.nixfmt is now what pkgs.nixfmt-rfc-style used to name; nixfmt-classic is the pre-RFC-166 tool; nixpkgs-fmt (a different, nix-community tool) was archived 2024-07-24 and is now purely historical.

CVE-2026-39860 (critical, published 2026-04-07) is a bypass of the 2024 fix for CVE-2024-27297 — a sandbox-escape class of bug believed closed for two years was not; patched again in 2.34.5/2.33.4/2.32.7/2.31.4/2.30.4/2.29.3/2.28.6.

nixpkgs is actively adding module-system error contexts specifically to diagnose infinite-recursion in imports/module arguments (#370967), an implicit admission the plain 'infinite recursion encountered' message was insufficient.

finalAttrs.finalPackage is now nixpkgs's own documented canonical idiom for self-referential derivations (pkgs/by-name/README.md's worked example), sharpening H1's 'agents avoid rec' finding into a specific recommended replacement rather than just an avoidance.

candidates.why: Nix 2.35's own experimental-features page still lists flakes as experimental; RFC 136 stabilises the non-flake CLI first and defers flake stabilisation behind another future RFC — no date exists. Directly falsifies any 'flakes are stable now' claim.
nix flake lock --update-input <name> was replaced by nix flake update [<name>...] in Nix 2.19 (2023-11-17); nix flake lock became add-only. Classic stale-training-data command agents still emit.
nix profile install was renamed nix profile add in Nix 2.30 (2025-07-07); old name kept only as alias.
Nix 2.26 (2025-01-22) added relative path: flake inputs, which is a lock-file-format-breaking change — pre-2.26 Nix cannot read a lock containing such a lock.

Nix 2.27 (2025-03-03) lets a flake declare inputs.self.submodules/inputs.self.lfs itself instead of forcing every consumer to pass submodules=true by hand — a real consumer-UX win most existing flakes don't use yet.
Nix 2.32 (2025-10-06) made nix flake check skip derivations that can be substituted instead of always building them, changing what a green CI check actually verifies.

Nix 2.33 (2025-12-09) explicitly labels nix registry resolve, full-input-type nix flake clone, and multithreaded git revCount as 'upstreamed from Determinate Nix' — shows Determinate Nix routinely runs ahead of CppNix.

Nix 2.35 (2026-06-22) makes flake/tarball source copies to the store lazy (~2x faster nixpkgs fetch/unpack), converging on the effect Determinate Nix's 'lazy trees' (3.6.7) delivered over a year earlier.

DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action's own README says it installs Determinate Nix by default, not upstream CppNix — surprising given the generic action name; a CI pipeline expecting vanilla Nix is silently on a fork.

determinate-nix-action is version-pinned to exact Determinate Nix releases and required for FlakeHub private-flake/cache access, while nix-installer-action always tracks 'most recent' even when the Action itself is pinned — a reproducibility gap a maintainer must know about.

GitHub replaced the Actions cache backend with an undocumented Twirp/Protobuf API on 2025-02-01, killing magic-nix-cache's free tier; a community fork revived magic-nix-cache-action (now v15, 2026-09-09) against the new API — pre-2025-02 advice needs re-verification, not blind trust.

flake-utils' last commit is 2024-11-13 and its own tracker carries an open, unresolved 'Potential feature-freeze or deprecation in favor of flake-parts' issue — yet eachDefaultSystem remains the most common idiom in the wild (H1 confirmed), so authoring guidance must actively steer people away, not wait for visible breakage.

nixfmt reached stable and became pkgs.nixfmt in nixpkgs 25.11 (2025-11), retiring the placeholder pkgs.nixfmt-rfc-style name; the pre-RFC-166 tool survives only as pkgs.nixfmt-classic. Any flake.nix still writing formatter.${system} = pkgs.nixfmt-rfc-style needs updating.
nix-community/nixpkgs-fmt is archived (confirmed via GitHub API), last commit 2024-07-24 — dead, still referenced in old tutorials, should not be recommended.

nix-community/nixd's last commit (2026-09-21) is materially fresher than oxalica/nil's (2026-07-26) — both alive, but nixd is the more actively maintained language server to default new devShell/editor config to.
Both statix (pushed 2026-07-26) and deadnix (last commit 2026-09-05) are actively maintained, contradicting an assumed-abandoned prior — safe to gate CI on either.
rustPlatform.buildRustPackage switched its default to fetchCargoVendor in nixpkgs 25.05, changing every cargoHash even without a version bump; cargoSha256 now hard-errors instead of merely warning.
buildGoModule requires env.CGO_ENABLED instead of direct CGO_ENABLED — warning in nixpkgs 25.05, hard error in 25.11; buildGoPackage was removed outright in 25.05.

substituteInPlace's --replace is deprecated in favour of --replace-fail/--replace-warn/--replace-quiet (tracking issue open since 2024-11-14, ~7000 in-tree holdouts) but NOT yet removed — a 'watch this' shift, not a completed one.

buildPythonPackage/buildPythonApplication switched their default updateScript to nix-update-script in nixpkgs 25.11 — an explicit nixpkgs statement that nix-update is the maintained update path, relevant to a flake's own release automation.
requireFile-derived packages default meta.license = unfree starting nixpkgs 26.11-unstable; a flake evaluating such packages now needs explicit unfree allowance where it previously didn't.

nixpkgs 25.11 raises the macOS minimum to Sonoma 14.0 and explicitly telegraphs an x86_64-darwin drop by 26.11 given Apple ending Intel-Mac OS updates — a systems-targeting decision a flake must make now.

Lix 2.95 (2026-03-25) forbids rec-set merges/dynamic attrs, requires a leading zero on floats, and removes builtins.fetchClosure entirely — CppNix still accepts all of these, so code only ever tested on CppNix can silently fail on Lix.
Lix has begun extracting Flakes out of its core into a plugin as of 2.95 — an in-progress structural divergence from CppNix's monolithic flakes implementation.

Determinate Nix's flake-schemas (3.17.0, a custom `schemas` output improving nix flake show) is Determinate-only and not confirmed to degrade gracefully on plain CppNix, which doesn't understand the attribute.

H2's core UX gap: community discussion confirms duplicate nixpkgs instances in flake.lock are a real, reported pain point, but no canonical detection command (vs. reading flake.lock by eye) is established — a rule needs a verification command here.

Adding a follows edit to flake.nix without re-running nix flake update leaves flake.lock showing the old input as a separate node — a confirmed, reported failure mode with no widely known one-line fix.

GitHub's Feb-2025 Actions-cache API replacement broke magic-nix-cache specifically; whether other Nix caching actions (e.g. cache-nix-action) share the same backend risk is unconfirmed in this wave and needs checking before recommending any GHA-cache-backed action.

Whether nix flake check --no-build actually validates devShells/checks outputs or only packages is a directly testable claim this survey's own toolchain could verify but did not fully — a concrete verification-command gap for a future rule.

H8: nixConfig in flake.nix (extra substituters/trusted keys) is ignored for untrusted users and prompts on accept-flake-config, a security/UX trap flagged but not independently re-verified this wave — high-value for the flake-authoring corpus.
candidates.source: nix-frame.md H8 (orchestrator hypothesis, unverified this wave)

candidates.why: Given flakes remain experimental (RFC 136) and lock-format has already broken once mid-window (2.26 relative paths), what compatibility promise a published flake can make about flake.lock schema stability across a Nix upgrade is an open, unanswered design question a release skill needs.
The nixexprs.tar.xz tarball is scheduled for discontinuation after nixpkgs 27.05 (2027-12-31) in favour of .tar.zst — anyone pulling nixpkgs via channels.nixos.org needs to plan the swap.

cachix/install-nix-action (latest v31.11.1, 2026-08-13) installs upstream CppNix while both DeterminateSystems actions install Determinate Nix — a real fork in what implementation a CI runner ends up on depending purely on which action a workflow picked.

The git-fetcher's 2.33 libgit2/threading rewrite and 2.35's lazy source copies both touch when revCount/lastModified metadata becomes available during evaluation — directly relevant to H4's ad hoc self.shortRev-based flake versioning, and untested this wave.

recent_shifts: nix flake update replaces nix flake lock --update-input (Nix 2.19, 2023-11-17) — outside the 18-24mo window but still live muscle-memory trap
nix profile install renamed to nix profile add (Nix 2.30, 2025-07-07)

FlakeHub rolling-vs-tagged semver visibility bug, documented July 2026 (package mist, imTHAI/nix-packages): once a real tag ≥0.2.0 exists, every subsequent 0.1.<commit-count> rolling release becomes permanently invisible to unpinned latest consumers — invalidates 'rolling releases are simpler, just use them'.
nixpkgs 26.11 dropped x86_64-darwin support (per its own release notes, cited in nix-vscode-extensions' README) — any generator advice for 'all Darwin systems' written pre-26.11 now over-promises.

Terraform's BSL relicense forced nixpkgs-terraform to flip its default allowUnfree starting at its own v4.0.0, threaded per underlying-Terraform-version rather than repo-wide — a generator's unfree/license posture is not a one-time decision.

rust-overlay tightened its own retention window to 'not earlier than {current_year-1}-01-01' to control repo size — invalidates 'never delete, keep every historical entry forever' as a universal policy at zig-overlay's scale.

CI installer actions across the corpus are uniformly pinned (cachix/install-nix-action@v31, nixbuild/nix-quick-install-action@v34) with explicit nix_version pins — none of the eight generators rely on an unpinned 'latest Nix' install action, consistent with H9.

flake-checker 0.2.15 (confirmed by running it against the pinned toolchain) exposes --check-outdated/--check-owner/--check-supported specifically to lint a flake's own nixpkgs-input drift — a fairly recent (post-2024) practice none of the eight exemplars' own CI actually runs yet.
